problem:
Compute $P(-1\le X\le 2)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{10}({x}^{2}+1),\, & -2\le x\le 1, \\ \frac{1}{20} & 1<x\le 9, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a\le X\le b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1\le X\le 2) & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{1}{10}({x}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{20}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{10}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+x]}_{-1}^{1}+{[\frac{1}{20}x]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}([\frac{1}{3}(1)^{3}+1]-[\frac{1}{3}(-1)^{3}+(-1)])+\frac{1}{20}(2-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{10}(\frac{8}{3})+\frac{1}{20} \\  & =\frac{4}{15}+\frac{1}{20} \\  & =\frac{19}{60}.\end{aligned}
$$
